notes: Experimental numbers are template fields resolved only from the owner's selected original results/*.json. No model calls during production. Educational dates and counts have their own cited sources.
lines: race-intro
这张图，你一眼就认出来了。
You probably recognize this picture before you have even finished looking at it.
race-intro
现在，把它交给四个程序：这是七吗？
Now give the same picture to four programs. Ask each one: is this a seven?
race-run
准备好了吗？一起按下开始。
Ready? Let's start their clocks together and watch what happens.
race-result
X 已经答完了，只用了 {x_us} 微秒。
X has already finished. Its time is {x_us} microseconds per picture.
terminal
这是实验留下的原始记录。
These are the original result files saved from the experiment.
race-result
换了{test_n_zh}张没见过的图，X 全都答对。
Across {test_n_en} pictures it had never trained on, X got every answer right.
ratio-claude
它比 Claude Fable 快了约 {claude_million_zh} 万倍。
It was about {claude_million_en} million times faster than Claude Fable.
ratio-astra
比 GPT-6-Astra，还快了 {astra_ten_million_zh} 多万倍。
And over {astra_ten_million_en} million times faster than GPT-6-Astra.
mystery
这个藏着名字的 X，到底是谁？
So who is this mysterious X, with its name still hidden from us?
title
一个一九五七年的 AI，比 ChatGPT Astra 和 Claude Fable 还快？
A 1957 AI model is faster than ChatGPT Astra and Claude Fable?
time-travel
先回到一九五七年，桌上只留纸和笔。
Let's go back to 1957. For now, all we need is paper and a pencil.
heart-photo
电脑没有眼睛，怎么把一张图交给它？
A computer has no eyes like ours. How can we give it a picture?
heart-mosaic
把画面切成小方格，每格只留一种颜色。
Divide the picture into little squares, and keep just one color in each square.
heart-bits
再简单一点，黑的写一，白的写零。
Make it simpler still: write one for black, and zero for white.
worksheet-heart
你念一排数字，让孩子照着涂。
Read a row of numbers aloud. Let your child color the squares to match.
worksheet-heart
先别告诉他是什么，看看他什么时候猜出来。
Keep the picture a secret for a moment. See when your child recognizes it.
cat-photo
现在换这只猫，先看照片。
Now try this cat. Here is the photograph before we turn it into squares.
cat-mosaic
格子越大，毛和胡须就越难看清。
As the squares get bigger, the fur and whiskers become harder to make out.
cat-bits
只剩八行，猫的耳朵还在。
Eventually there are only eight rows left. Can you still spot the cat's ears?
cat-bytes
每行八个零和一，刚好装进一个字节。
Each row has eight zeros and ones. That fits neatly inside one byte.
cat-bytes
整只猫，只占八个字节。
So the whole tiny cat takes just eight bytes to store.
worksheet-cat
把数字寄给朋友，他也能在纸上还原出来。
Send those numbers to a friend. They can rebuild your cat on paper, square by square.
neuron
纸上的格子有了，谁来做决定呢？
We have our squares. But how can something make a decision from them?
neuron
先借大脑里的一个神经元来想想。
Let's borrow a very simple idea from a neuron in the brain.
neuron
它收到许多信号，有些强，有些弱。
A neuron receives many signals. Some connections have a stronger effect than others.
neuron-fire
合起来够了，它就发出一次信号。
When the combined input is enough, it sends a signal of its own.
neuron-many
人脑大约有八百六十亿个神经元。
The human brain is often estimated to contain about eighty-six billion neurons.
neuron-many
我们先拿一个很简单的模型，玩个游戏。
We can start with a much simpler model, and turn it into a game.
apple-red
假装你是个神经元，要找出苹果。
Pretend you are a neuron. Your job is to decide whether something is an apple.
apple-round
红色加一分，圆形也加一分。
Give it one point for being red, and another point for being round.
apple-light
够两分，就举起手，表示找到了。
When it gets two points, raise your hand. That means you think you found one.
tomato
可番茄也能拿满分，怎么办？
But a tomato can collect both points too. What could you change?
apple-clue
再加一条线索：吃起来甜不甜？
Try another clue: does it taste sweet? How much should that clue count?
hebb
赫布早就提出，常一起活动的连接会变强。
Back in 1949, Hebb proposed that repeated activity together could strengthen connections.
lab-3
现在，把打分的游戏放进网页里。
Now let's move our little points game into the browser laboratory.
lab-3
每个格子，都有一个自己的分数。
Every square in the picture has its own points value, ready to be adjusted.
lab-round
点一下 Run one round，看看它怎么学。
Click Run one round, and watch the points while it works through the examples.
lab-round
横线应该亮灯，它却没亮，就得加分。
If a horizontal line should switch the light on and does not, add points.
lab-round
只给这张图里黑着的格子加分。
Only change the points for squares that are black in this particular picture.
lab-points
下面那串 points，也跟着一起变。
Look underneath the grid. The numbers in the points list change at the same time.
lab-points
反过来，多亮了，就把对应的分数减一点。
If the light comes on when it should stay off, lower those points instead.
lab-20
格子换成二十乘二十，方法还是一样。
Now switch to a twenty-by-twenty picture. The learning rule stays just the same.
lab-20
练完以后，蓝色的分数像不像一个七？
After training, do the blue points begin to remind you of a seven?
code-predict
predict 只管把黑格子的分数加起来。
The predict function adds up the points belonging to the black squares.
code-train
train 对照答案，决定分数要不要改。
The train function checks the answer and decides whether those points need changing.
code-both
人给它看例子，具体的分数让它自己调。
We supply examples and answers. The program adjusts the individual points as it learns.
reveal
现在可以揭晓了：X 就是感知机。
Now we can reveal X. It is a perceptron.
report
罗森布拉特在一九五七年写下了这套想法。
Frank Rosenblatt described his perceptron ideas in a report published in 1957.
mark-eye
后来的 Mark I，真有一块光电管做的眼睛。
The later Mark I machine had an eye made from a grid of light sensors.
mark-eye
排成二十乘二十，把卡片的明暗读进去。
Those sensors were arranged in a twenty-by-twenty array, reading light and dark from a card.
mark-motors
要改连接的强弱，电机就转动电位器。
To adjust a connection's strength, a small motor physically turned a potentiometer.
mark-output
学完再放进卡片，输出灯就给出答案。
After learning, another card could be presented, and the output indicated the machine's decision.
vintage-lab
它的记忆，真的留在那些旋钮的位置上。
The positions of those adjustable controls physically stored what the machine had learned.
newspaper
当年的报纸说，这台机器能从做中学。
A 1958 newspaper headline described a new Navy device that learns by doing.
reveal-code
比赛里的 X，用 JavaScript 写了简化的规则。
Our race used a simplified perceptron rule written in JavaScript and running on this Mac.
reveal-trained
它已经看过 {train_n} 张训练图，再来参加比赛。
It had already learned from {train_n} training pictures before entering the race.
scale
它为什么这么快？现在看看它要做多少事。
Why was it so fast? Now we can look at how much work it actually does.
scale
一张图，最多只要把 {pixel_n} 个分数加一遍。
For one picture, it needs at most {pixel_n} additions to collect the points.
scale-zoom
本机那个 Qwen 模型，有大约八十亿个参数。
The local Qwen model has roughly eight billion parameters, a much larger collection of numbers.
scale-zoom
它要一层层计算，再一个词一个词地往外写。
It computes through layers, then produces its answer a token at a time.
timeline-1957
从这个简单的神经元，后来长出了更复杂的网络。
This simple artificial neuron was part of a much longer story of increasingly complex networks.
timeline-1969
一九六九年，一本书仔细研究了感知机的局限。
In 1969, Minsky and Papert published a detailed mathematical study of perceptrons and their limitations.
timeline-1986
后来研究冷过一阵。反向传播让多层网络更好学。
Interest later cooled for a time. Backpropagation helped make networks with multiple layers learn effectively.
timeline-2012
到二零一二年，深度网络的认图成绩提高了很多。
In 2012, a deep neural network made a major breakthrough in the ImageNet picture-recognition competition.
timeline-2017
接着是 Transformer，再到今天会聊天的 AI。
Then came the Transformer, followed by the conversational AI systems we use today.
chat
大模型能聊的事，远远超过这道认图题。
Those models can discuss far more than this one small question about a picture.
limits
可简单的事，它也可能算得很费力。
Even a simple request can still require a great deal of computation.
limits
这次本机的 Qwen，只答对了{qwen_right_zh}张。
In this experiment, the local Qwen model answered only {qwen_right_en} of the pictures correctly.
limits
回答很有把握，也不一定就是真的。
And an answer that sounds confident is still something we may need to check.
family
这些实验，在家里的餐桌上就能开始。
You can begin exploring these ideas right at your own family table.
family
打印一张格子纸，拿几支笔就够了。
Print a worksheet, find a few pencils, and leave some room for trying things out.
family
一个人念数字，另一个人把图涂出来。
One person reads the numbers, while someone else colors in the hidden picture.
start
再轮流当神经元，商量每条线索值几分。
Then take turns being the neuron. Decide together how much each clue should count.
start
想让机器来试，就打开网页里的实验室。
When you want the computer to try, open the browser lab and teach it with examples.
url
网址稍后公布，学习单也会放在一起。
The website address will be announced soon, with the printable worksheets in the same place.
invite
来 Lucas Academy 一起试试：你和孩子想先教它认什么？
Come explore with us at Lucas Academy. What would you and your child like to teach it to recognize first?
